description.p: Machines manages the QEMU/KVM virtual machines of a libvirt connection, the system one or your user session, built with GTK 4 and libadwaita.

ul.li: Start, shut down, pause, save to disk, reboot and force off machines, and follow their state as it changes

A built-in VNC and SPICE console that scales the guest's display to the window and passes the keyboard and pointer through, with sound, clipboard sharing, USB redirection and 3D acceleration over SPICE
A serial console shown as text
New machines from an installation ISO or an existing disk image, with a disk in libvirt's default storage pool, set up for the system on the ISO
Processors, memory, autostart, boot order and the CD-ROM drive changed from the details page
Graphs of what a running machine uses of the host's processors, memory, disks and network
Processor model, topology and pinning, huge pages, and BIOS or UEFI firmware with Secure Boot
Machines renamed, and cloned with copies of their disks
Snapshots of a machine's disks, and of its memory while it runs, to revert to
Disks, CD/DVD drives, network interfaces, display and video card, and USB and PCI devices of the host added and changed from the details page
Storage pools, disks of the host and virtual networks
A machine's XML definition, edited by hand

description.p: New virtual machines boot with the firmware chosen for them: BIOS, UEFI, or UEFI with Secure Boot, which is the default where the host's firmware has it, as Windows 11 requires. Their disk goes in the storage pool chosen for it, which shows its free space, and their processors are cores of one socket, so that Windows uses all of them.

The serial console is offered only to machines with a serial port, which is added and removed with the other devices. The sidebar selects a machine on a click, no longer as the pointer passes over it. Fullscreen works from any page, with F11 too, and going back to the list leaves it. The user session explains why it has no virtual networks instead of failing to make one, and a keyboard shortcuts dialog lists what the keyboard does.
